scope: Storage-only trials using 384 sampled committed Flink decisions, with remapped identities and recomputed input hashes. All sampled decisions were APPROVE.
notes: One 100000-row backlog trial per mode, in PostgreSQL/raw1/mv1/mv3 order; results include consumer startup and polling granularity. Warm-cache and ordering effects are not controlled.
PostgreSQL performs authoritative identity/content checks and maintains more read models. ClickHouse stores deliveries without equivalent business acceptance checks.
PostgreSQL materializer and producer each had 1 CPU; databases 2 CPUs/2 GiB each; Connect 1 CPU/1 GiB except the explicitly marked 2-CPU trial; Keeper had a separate 1 CPU/512 MiB budget.

The initial live500 trial was interrupted by host disk exhaustion and is excluded. Its damaged ClickHouse raw/MV/aggregate tables were marked detached with files retained. Completed backlog tables reconciled after restart.
The first 5000/s trial overlapped local Java validation; the sink_final1 repeat did not. Both grew backlog. The 2-CPU trial also had substantial generator scheduling delay.

Live tests run for 60 monotonic seconds. Timestamp-based latency and acknowledgement alignment are exploratory on this shared WSL host; wall-clock sample spans show drift relative to monotonic producer duration.
Publish-to-insert latency in backlog/retry cases includes waiting between experiments and must not be treated as live latency.
Progress uses metadata or indexed topic totals; complete verification scans are restricted to each isolated benchmark table.
Recovery after the first fault required a setting change and explicit failed-task restart. The second fault stopped at BEFORE_PROCESSING; no offsets were manually advanced.
Keeper/table mismatch after disk data loss requires rebuilding target/group/Keeper state consistently from retained Kafka or a backup. Process restart tests do not qualify disk-loss recovery.
